name: Spiss
kurzbeschreibung: Highest-altitude settlement in the district of Landeck, near the Swiss border, offering solitude and breathtaking mountain scenery.
beschreibung:
Spiss lies at an elevation of 1,740 meters in the district of Landeck, not far from the Swiss border at the entrance to the Samnauntal – and is thus the highest permanently inhabited settlement in the district. The hamlet with its roughly 100 inhabitants nestles on a sun-exposed high plateau between the Gribellekopf and the Pezinerspitz, with an open view toward Engadin and Silvretta. Anyone who comes here leaves the bustle of the Inntal far behind: the narrow road winds steeply up from Pfunds, and once you arrive at the top, one thing above all is noticeable – silence.

Hiking is the main thing in Spiss. The village is a starting point for tours into the surrounding mountain world, for example to the Frudigerjochhütte or up toward the Gribellekopf, where you stand at 2,500 meters among chamois and alpine roses. In winter, the cross-country ski trail runs from here into Swiss Samnaun, and ski tourers use the untouched slopes around the village. Particularly characteristic is the location at the tri-border area Österreich–Schweiz–Italien, which has always made Spiss, despite its remoteness, a small hub of alpine transit routes.

When it comes to food, Spiss offers honest Tiroler fare – Graukasnocken and Kaspressknödel in simple inns, often with products from the surrounding farms' own livestock operations. Anyone seeking absolute quiet, far from well-trodden tourism paths, is in the right place here. 🌲
